title: Dagobert Renouf on Twitter growth: small goals, personal brands, and not quitting channels too early
summary: Dagobert Renouf (Logology founder) explains why big ambition causes perfectionism and how focusing on small goals gets him shipping. He covers why personal brands beat company accounts, why repeating content kills Twitter engagement, and why channels like affiliates need time before you judge them.

principles.text: Keep big dreams but focus on small goals; they keep you executing instead of paralyzed.
principles.quote: have small goals like keep having Big Dreams to like focus on like small goals

principles.text: An outsized ambition fuels perfectionism, because you try to guarantee an outcome you can't guarantee.
principles.quote: if I was stuck in this ambition I would be stuck in perfectionism to try to reassure myself that it's gonna be achieved

principles.text: Avoid both extremes: don't polish forever, and don't launch a weekend project and quit. Give a validated idea a real go.
principles.quote: maybe it's good to spend one month or two months on something if you have some pre-validation some hints it can work

principles.text: Don't give up on an acquisition channel too soon; it can take months to pay off, but change what isn't working.
principles.quote: if you give up too soon like I could have stopped the affiliation after three months and say oh I don't want to keep you know losing 30 a month but now it's making us like 400 a month

principles.text: If you build products around one topic, build a personal brand rather than a company account; it's far easier to grow.
principles.quote: basically it's 10 times easier to build an audience for a person than for a brand that's obvious because it's like people relate

principles.text: Repeating the same content wears out your audience; keep your content fresh and evolve it after the first year.
principles.quote: if I make the same joke a hundred times eventually it's less funny and it's it's normal you know like people get bored
